alignments.note: Rectum takes the *of* and the supplied *the* (rules 19 and 46).
Predicate noun with the construction-supplied copula and its own *an* (rules 20 and 15).
*How much more* is what the ASV spends on this particle's a-fortiori force; headed on the comparative word (rule 24).
כִּי takes the *when* the ASV writes at the head of its clause; splitting it from אַף is preferred to fusing the pair, since each morpheme has a rendering of its own (rules 2 and 30).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
One substantive rendered by a multi-word phrase; the head is the word whose loss loses the lexeme, the generic *mind* being supplied (rule 31), with the *a* joining the expression (rule 15).

review_notes: Fusing אַף כִּי into a single *How much more when* unit was the competing analysis; the split was taken because each morpheme owns a distinct part of the English (rule 30's subtraction test).
The margin's *Or, to atone for wickedness* was read and set aside (rule 38).
